title: Sign-optimized Quantum Monte Carlo
authors: Julius S. Herz, Robin Schäfer, Matías G. Gonzalez, David J. Luitz
abstract: The sign problem breaks the polynomial scaling of Quantum Monte Carlo methods. We alleviate it by rotation of the local basis of the Hilbert space, such that the phase of off-diagonal matrix elements of the rotated Hamiltonian is minimized. These minima coincide with optima of the average sign. We benchmark our method for frustrated Heisenberg antiferromagnets in one dimension and on the two-dimensional maple-leaf lattice. Our approach reveals more efficient bases with improved sign in a large part of the parameter space for all models considered, enabling us to reach lower temperatures, on par with state-of-the-art numerical linked cluster expansions which we directly compare to.
summary: This paper introduces a novel basis optimization technique to alleviate the sign problem plaguing Quantum Monte Carlo simulations. By systematically rotating the local Hilbert space basis based on minimizing non-stoquasticity, the authors achieve improved simulation accuracy and reach lower temperatures for frustrated magnetic models. This provides a powerful new computational tool for studying strongly correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the sign problem in Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, which causes exponential statistical fluctuations for certain quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors developed a basis optimization technique that significantly mitigates the sign problem by rotating the local Hilbert space basis, enabling simulations at lower temperatures than previous state-of-the-art methods.
method: The method involves optimizing the local basis via unitary rotations, guided by minimizing a generalized non-stoquasticity measure ($S(U)$), which is hypothesized to coincide with maximizing the average sign ($\langle s angle$).
model_or_system: The approach is benchmarked on frustrated Heisenberg antiferromagnets on lattices such as the one-dimensional chain, the two-dimensional maple-leaf lattice (MLL), and ladder systems.
key_observables: Average Sign ($\langle s angle$), Non-stoquasticity ($S(U)$), Specific Heat Capacity.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$) and various coupling strengths defining the magnetic interactions ($J$).
main_assumptions: The optimization relies on the assumption that minimizing non-stoquasticity guides the system toward maximizing the average sign, although this is noted to be a sufficient but not necessary condition for solving the problem.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate computational phase diagrams showing optimal basis changes across coupling strengths (MLL), and plots comparing $\langle s angle$ versus $S(U)$ for different ladder systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the sign problem in SSE-QMC to proposing a general unitary basis rotation scheme, detailing the two-stage optimization process (Adam/LBFGS), and finally benchmarking this technique on specific frustrated lattice models.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the core methodology—systematic numerical optimization of simulation representations using advanced gradient descent techniques—is highly relevant to developing robust computational tools for complex quantum systems in AMO physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: (Left) Maple-leaf lattice with its three symmetry-inequivalent couplings: Jd (amber) along dimers, Jt (teal) along triangles, and Jh (blue) along hexagons. (Right) Computational phase diagram of the MLL for T = 0.5J: the color indicates the basis with the largest average QMC sign (computational/dimer/trimer eigen- basis in blue/amber/teal; optimized 2-spin/3-spin clustering in purple/red) on an N = 54 site lattice. The transparency indicates the average sign. The isotropic point Jh = Jt = Jd is marked by the black star.

Figure 2: (Left) average QMC sign 〈s〉as a function of the generalized non- stoquasticity S(UA, UB) along the optimization trajectory for the fully-frustrated lad- der (shown in the inset) of N = 24 sites at T = J. (Right) the same for the triangular ladder.

Figure 3: (Left) Average sign against temperature for the triangular ladder system simulated in bases resulting from the optimization with randomly distributed initial conditions. For each class of bases we plot one sign–temperature curve. For compari- son, the sign-temperature curves for the computational basis and the rung eigenbasis are also plotted. (Right) Energy obtained from QMC simulations in the same bases. The black line represents the ED result for an N = 12 lattice. The simulations are performed on an N = 24 triangular ladder.

Figure 4: (Left) Sign gradient at the middle and end points of the optimization pro- cedure. (Right) Non-stoquasticity gradient at the middle and end points of the opti- mization procedure. (Middle) Comparison between the two gradients at the middle point of the optimization (data taken from the left and right panels). Every point i represents a component of the gradient in the 32-dimensional space defined by the parametrization (see main text). We choose ε = 0.075. The simulations are per- formed on an N = 20 triangular ladder at T = J.

Figure 5: Average QMC sign for the maple-leaf lattice on the (θ,φ) grid, obtained from simulations in three different bases at T = 1.2 and 0.6. The lattice consists of N = 54 sites with periodic boundary conditions (see Appendix E for the full cluster). The limiting cases of free dimers (θ = 0), free trimers (θ = π/2,φ = 0), and the honeycomb lattice (φ = π/2) are indicated in white.
